summary: Health-probe flood triggering elevated 5xx and runtime restart cycles for dedicated tenant
description:
Issue summary:
Customer LexaAssist observed a sudden spike in 5xx responses (primarily 502/503) across their Dedicated pool for ~12 minutes. Multiple serving-runtime pods for the tenant entered restart cycles. The API Gateway returned elevated upstream 502s while the runtime reported high file-descriptor and connection counts.

Impact:
- Duration: 2026-03-14T09:12 - 2026-03-14T09:24 UTC (approx 12 minutes)
- Customer-reported impact: All inference requests returning 5xx, severe service disruption for LexaAssist live users.
- Observed error rate: peak 5xx rate ~31% of ingress requests for the tenant; overall cluster 5xx bump ~4%.

Environment:
- Deployment: Dedicated tenant pool (LexaAssist-prod), prod-us-west (us-west-2)
- Affected services: api-gateway (edge), edge-proxy (LB health checks), serving-runtime (gpu nodes)
- Models in flight: redwood-gpt-7b-quant (pinned for tenant)

Steps to reproduce (observed sequence):
1) Health probes (TCP/HTTP) from edge-proxy begin sending frequent concurrent probe requests to runtime admin/health endpoint due to an LB health-probe flapping incident following a control-plane redeploy.
2) Probe concurrency spikes (see logs) cause many short-lived connections directly to runtime admin + metrics port, bypassing normal token-based rate limits.
3) Runtime threads allocate extra resources to respond to probes and open ephemeral connections; kernel fd and memory pressure rises.
4) Under additional customer traffic, the runtime process crosses a resilience threshold and triggers internal restarts (watchdog).
5) API Gateway fails fast on upstream connection errors -> 502/503 observed at customer.

Logs / telemetry excerpts:
- edge-proxy logs: "healthcheck: concurrent probes=120 -> target=runtime-admin:5043"
- runtime metrics (pod r-03c): "active_fds=8192, open_connections=10240, rss=7.6GB"
- k8s events: "Back-off restarting failed container" repeated 8 times between 09:15-09:21 UTC
- api-gateway: "upstream connect error or reset, connection_reset", 502 returned to client

Investigation notes / hypotheses:
- Initial hypothesis: standard request burst or model hot-loop. Rejected: request body patterns did not match heavy token-generation workloads.
- Observed correlation between a spike in healthprobe traffic and the onset of fd/conn pressure on the runtime pods.
- Edge control-plane rollout around 09:10 UTC introduced a mis-scheduled health-probe reconnection behavior (probe interval temporarily reduced to 1s for some LB instances).
- Rate-limiting rules for health probes were not applied at the edge for admin endpoints, causing probe fanout to reach per-tenant runtime instances.
- Restart cycles were caused by connection exhaustion and the runtime watchdog killing processes that hit fd limits.

Actions taken / mitigation (timeline):
- 09:14 UTC: Support triaged and paged SRE and Dedicated runtime on-call.
- 09:16 UTC: Throttled health checks at edge: applied temporary probe-shedding rule to limit concurrent probes per target to 10 (edge-proxy hotfix).
- 09:18 UTC: Disabled problematic LB instance that was reintroducing 1s probe interval (rolled back control-plane change).
- 09:19 UTC: Manually drained affected runtime pods and allowed autoscaler to replace them into healthy state.
- 09:22 UTC: API Gateway rate-limiter temporarily increased upstream retry timeout to reduce client-side 502 amplification.
- 09:24 UTC: Error rates returned to baseline; customer traffic restored.

Resolution / root cause:
- Root cause: A control-plane rollout caused a subset of LB instances to temporarily reduce health-probe intervals to 1 second. Health probes were not constrained by edge-level probe-shedding rules for admin endpoints, producing a probe flood (concurrent probes > 100) against tenant runtime admin ports. This led to fd/connection exhaustion on runtime processes and subsequent restart loops.
- Permanent fix deployed: (a) enforce probe-shedding at edge for admin/health endpoints (PR #4123), (b) update control-plane rollout to prevent aggressive probe reconnection behavior, and (c) add alert for probe concurrency > 25 per target. PR link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/4123

Workaround provided to customer:
- Rerouted LexaAssist traffic to a warm standby Dedicated pool while we remediated the affected pool. Provided rollback window and verified model behaviour on standby.

Follow-ups / action items:
- SRE: Add a probe-concurrency monitor and PagerDuty rule for health-probe fanout.
- Edge team: Harden edge-proxy config to ensure probe-shedding applies to admin ports by default.
- Runtime team: Add guardrails for fd limits (graceful degradation path rather than immediate watchdog kill).
- Postmortem: Draft postmortem page and publish within 72 hours; link in Confluence.

References and artifacts:
- edge-proxy logs (bucket): s3://redwood-support/lexaassist/2026-03-14/edge-proxy-09-12.tgz
- runtime pod logs: /var/logs/k8s/lexaassist/r-03c.log (attached to ticket)
